01_repository_summary.title: Repository Summary
01_repository_summary.what_repository_does: Some directories have a tests folder. If it exists, go to that folder and run docker-compose up --build to build and run the docker image. The tests do not test all functionality of the docker images. They only serve as a small check that the docker image is built-able and can perform the most basic of tasks. You can run the /linting/do-linting.sh script (taking the base directory to lint as its only parameter) to check your code for issues that will potentially block pull request checks. The script will automatically use the .yamllint and .tflint.hcl config files used in PR checks, which are found in the /linting directory. Note that jsonlint may install as jsonlint depending on the method used, but the expected executable is jsonlint-php. If you have jsonlint on your system, symlink it to jsonlint-php to run this script. Note that you cannot symlink the do-linting.sh script because the check for config files will fail. However, it may be useful to add an executable script on your path that runs that script from its native directory.
